owner_request: 2026-10-14, in chat: 'are we sure everything is correct and not shallowly implementing ideas. can we not use AI/ML stuff to make the connections'
why_this_exists: A19's TNIC links are word-count cosine similarities. The owner asked whether machine learning would make better connections. Hoberg & Phillips (JF 2025) publish ETNIC: the same network built from a 300-dimension doc2vec embedding of each 10-K Item 1, which they report explains peer fundamentals 20-25% better than TNIC. Its readme (read before registering) states a separate doc2vec model is trained each year on that year's filings only, so it has no look-ahead. If A19 failed because word-count links were too shallow, ETNIC should show it.
data: ETNIC-3 (Etnic3_data.zip, Hoberg-Phillips Data Library, preliminary release; 1989-2023). Same mapping, timing, prices, liquidity and SIC as A19.

trials.T1_all_embedding_peers_1m: A19's T1 on ETNIC-3: all peers, score-weighted, 21-day return, 1-month horizon
trials.T2_non_sic3_embedding_peers_1m: A19's T2 on ETNIC-3: peers outside the firm's SIC3 only

measurement_and_pass_rule: A19's word for word, via scripts/run_network_peer_screen_v1.py; positive control (same-month co-movement vs random partners) reported first
cumulative_search_note: These two re-test A19's T1 and T2 on a different network; they are counted as new trials, on top of A19's four.
known_weaknesses_declared_up_front: Preliminary release; Hoberg-Phillips may adjust boilerplate purging. The download timestamp is recorded.
ETNIC also covers firms without a CRSP link; only firms in our price panel enter, as with A19.
